principles: Preserve the rev-1 honesty scaffolding (claim boundary, pre-registration, immutable ledger, mechanical isolation, no-overclaim) — the review confirmed it is load-bearing
Every correction must trace to one of the 12 adjudicated findings; no new design invention beyond them
Name and reuse existing components (hint-mode, recovery-runner, analyze.mjs) instead of describing greenfield builds
Factual claims about the codebase must match source-verified reality (INIT review confirmed each)
Entirely English; docs-only; milestones remain future stories
drivers: The rev-1 file no longer exists on disk (deleted mid-review), so restoration requires authoring, not patching
Three validity holes (circularity, store pollution, fixture leakage) would invalidate any run of the rev-1 design
The operator explicitly scoped this as a docs story restoring the corrected plan only

options.name: clean-reauthor-rev2
pros: Single coherent document; corrections integrated in-place where they belong
No risk of resurrecting rev-1 errors verbatim
Cheaper than reconstructing the deleted draft then diffing 12 multi-section changes
cons: Reviewers cannot diff against rev-1 on disk (mitigated: revision-provenance header lists what changed and why)

options.name: restore-rev1-then-patch
pros: Produces an explicit rev-1→rev-2 diff for reviewers
cons: Requires committing a known-invalid rev-1 first (validity holes on record as current guidance, even if briefly)
Two commits and double review surface for a file that was never committed to begin with
The 12 corrections touch most of the 18 sections, so the diff would approximate a rewrite anyway

options.name: corrections-appendix-only
cons: Leaves the invalid rev-1 design text as the primary reading; an executor following the body would still build the 588-task invalid study
Contradicts the review verdict that design parameters and geometry must change, not be footnoted

rationale: The draft was never committed and no longer exists on disk, so there is no on-disk baseline to patch; a clean rev-2 authoring with a revision-provenance header integrates all 12 corrections coherently without ever publishing the known-invalid rev-1 design as current guidance.

preMortem.scenario: The rev-2 document misstates an existing-component fact (path, API, or behavior) that the plan depends on
preMortem.trigger: Authoring from session memory instead of the source-verified facts list
preMortem.consequence: A future milestone story builds against a wrong integration point; the plan loses credibility as a decision doc
preMortem.mitigation: Every component claim in the doc traces to the understanding facts the INIT reviewer verified in source (hint-mode.ts parity, experience-hint-surface render-gate, resolveLearningRoot canonicalization, recovery-runner mkdtemp, analyze.mjs primitives); REVIEW lanes re-verify

preMortem.scenario: Chinese characters or CJK punctuation slip into the document
preMortem.trigger: Copy-paste from the bilingual review conversation
preMortem.mitigation: Author from the English scratchpad draft only; grep the final file for CJK ranges before commit

preMortem.scenario: The document drifts beyond the 12 adjudicated corrections into new design decisions
preMortem.trigger: Filling gaps discovered while writing (e.g. inventing new metrics or milestones)
preMortem.consequence: Un-reviewed design enters a decision doc under a docs-only story, bypassing the adversarial review that validated the 12
preMortem.mitigation: Scope check: every substantive rev-1→rev-2 delta maps to a numbered finding; anything else is flagged as a follow-up story instead of written in

preMortem.scenario: Concurrent repo activity recreates or renames the same file while this story is in flight
preMortem.trigger: Another host restores its own copy of the deleted draft
preMortem.consequence: Merge conflict or duplicate competing plans in decisions/
preMortem.mitigation: Story branch owns the single allowed path; before DONE merge, re-check main for a competing file and reconcile explicitly rather than auto-merging
